elements.evidence: The rendered clause retains a covenant binding Customer: "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party who is directly involved in performing services under this Agreement". Customer therefore remains subject to a non-solicit, so the preferred position (deletion of the covenant as to Customer) is not achieved. The drafter deliberately targeted the fallback to avoid orphaning the Article XI injunctive-relief cross-reference.

Operative sentence now reads "neither party will solicit any person employed by the other party ... to leave his or her employment with that party", replacing the one-way "the Licensee will not solicit any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates". Both directions are bound.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Scope limited to "any person employed by the other party who is directly involved in performing services under this Agreement"; the original all-employee/Affiliate reach ("any person employed by Licensor and/or its Affiliates") is gone.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: "During the Term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after the end of a person's involvement in services under this Agreement" replaces the three-year post-termination tail; the post-involvement tail is capped at twelve months and is anchored to the end of that person's involvement, as the checklist requires.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained definition: "the term \"Solicit\" ... shall not mean generally advertising job openings".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Retained definition excludes "any activities that constitute follow-up to individuals who respond to job opening advertisements or who voluntarily initiate employment inquiries", covering unsolicited approaches.

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative verb is limited to "solicit", defined as "any affirmative recruitment specifically aimed at one or more individuals identified by name, title or affiliation"; there is no "employ or engage", "hire" or no-hire language anywhere in the clause.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: mutuality, involvement-based scope, a 12-month post-involvement tail, the two retained carve-outs and the absence of any hiring ban are all present in operative language rather than only promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not met and was not attempted; that is a legitimate choice here because deletion would leave the Article XI injunctive-relief reference to this covenant dangling, and a clause sitting at the fallback is acceptable under the playbook.

Minimality holds: only the single operative sentence was rewritten (party direction, personnel scope, duration). The "Solicit" definition sentence, which already supplies the advertising and unsolicited-inquiry carve-outs, is untouched, and no survival tail, remedy, procedure or extra covenant was added. Deleting "and/or its Affiliates" is inherent in the mutual, involvement-limited scope edit and is not a stray excision.
Intent preserved: the covenant, its "Solicit" definition, and the equitable-relief hook in Article XI all continue to function; no undefined term or broken cross-reference is created.

Residual tightening point (not an element failure, worth raising in negotiation): the retained opener "During the Term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after the end of a person's involvement" means a person whose involvement ends early in a long Term stays covered for the balance of the Term. If the counterparty resists, consider "for the period of a person's involvement in services under this Agreement and twelve (12) months thereafter" so the sole temporal anchor is the end of involvement.
